name: circle-graph
title: Circle on coordinate axes
tagline: A circle on numbered axes: derives the centre–radius equation, the tangent at a point (⊥ to the radius, exact equation) and where a line meets the circle.
description: A circle drawn on numbered, square coordinate axes — centred at the origin (x² + y² = r²) or at (a, b) — together with the coordinate-geometry of circles: mark a point on the circle, draw the radius to it and the tangent there (perpendicular to the radius, its equation derived in exact form), mark the radius⊥tangent right angle, and draw a straight line whose intersection point(s) with the circle are derived by solving the quadratic. You write only the circle (centre + radius), the points (their coordinates), and any lines (as equation strings); the circle equation, every point's exact on-circle position, the radius, the tangent and its equation, the right-angle mark and the line∩circle points are all computed. Occlude a point's coordinates, a tangent equation, the circle equation or the intersection coordinates to pose a question. v1 covers straight-line tangents and secants (not parabola∩circle, not two tangents from an external point).
whenToUse: Reach for this for the coordinate geometry of a circle on numbered axes: the equation of a circle (x² + y² = r² centred at the origin, or (x − a)² + (y − b)² = r² centred at (a, b)), the equation of a tangent to a circle at a given point, the fact that the radius is perpendicular to the tangent, and a line meeting a circle (solving the quadratic simultaneously — graphically). Author circle.center (default the origin [0, 0]) and circle.radius; the axes window auto-fits the circle if you omit axes. Add points: each point.at is the [x, y] coordinates of a point on the circle (choose lattice points so the figure is exact — e.g. (3, 4), (6, 8), (5, 12) on radius-5/10/13 circles, or (5, 5) on the circle centred (2, 1) radius 5); set point.radius to draw the radius to it, point.tangent to draw the tangent there, and the radius⊥tangent right angle is marked automatically when both are on. The tangent equation is shown next to the line — tangentForm "gradient-intercept" gives y = mx + c (default), "normal" gives the integer form px + qy = c, "both" shows each. Add lines: each lines[].expr is a straight-line equation string — "y = 2x + 1", "y = -x + 5", "x = 3", "2x + 3y = 12" — and the model marks where it cuts the circle (two points, one if the line is itself a tangent, none if it misses). Pose questions by occluding: point.occlude hides a point's coordinates as "(?, ?)"; point.occludeTangent hides its tangent equation; occludeEquation hides the circle equation; lines[].occludeIntersections hides the intersection coordinates. Leave a point with no tangent (and the equation hidden) as an answer space — "draw the tangent and find its equation". Set draggable to let pupils slide a point around the circle and watch the radius, the tangent and its equation stay perpendicular and update live. Keep the same window across a lesson so pupils track one diagram, and a staged build reads well (plot the circle → mark the point → draw the radius → draw the tangent → state the equation). Switch primitive when the teaching changes: a single curve y = f(x), its roots / turning points, use graphing/function-graph; a circle theorem (angle at the centre, cyclic quadrilateral, alternate segment, two tangents from a point) not on axes, use geometry/circle-theorems; arc length / sector or segment area, use geometry/circle-parts. Synonyms a teacher might use: equation of a circle, centre-radius form, tangent to a circle, equation of the tangent, radius perpendicular to tangent, line meets circle, points of intersection, circle and line, x squared plus y squared.

circle.description: The circle. Its equation and outline are derived; you give only its centre and radius.

center.description: Centre [a, b]. Default [0, 0] — the origin, giving x² + y² = r².

radius.description: Radius r (> 0). The equation x² + y² = r² (or (x − a)² + (y − b)² = r²) is derived from it.

centerLabel.description: Optional name for the centre (e.g. "C"), drawn beside the centre dot. Omit for an unlabelled centre; the origin needs none (the axes show 0).

axes.description: The window. OMIT to auto-fit a square window around the circle with a small margin. Always square-scaled so the circle is round.

step.description: Grid-line spacing. Default 1 so every lattice point sits on a crossing (helps read coordinates).

labelStep.description: Spacing of the numbers along the axes. Default: auto (a multiple of step coarse enough that the numbers do not crowd).

grid.description: Show the background grid. Default true.

points.description: Points ON the circle. Each is given by its coordinates; the position is snapped exactly onto the circle, and the radius, tangent and tangent equation are derived from it.

at.description: Coordinates [x, y] of a point on the circle. Pick a lattice point so the figure and the derived tangent equation are exact, e.g. (3, 4) on x² + y² = 25, or (5, 5) on (x − 2)² + (y − 1)² = 25.

label.description: Short name drawn beside the point, e.g. "P" or "A". Omit for none.

radius.description: Draw the radius (centre → point) as a dashed construction line. Default false.

tangent.description: Draw the tangent at this point (perpendicular to the radius). Its equation is shown unless occludeTangent or showTangentEquation false. Default false.

rightAngle.description: Mark the radius⊥tangent right angle. Defaults to true when BOTH radius and tangent are drawn; set false to suppress it.

showCoords.description: Show the (x, y) readout beside the point. Default true.

occlude.description: Hide this point's coordinates as "(?, ?)" — the "what are its coordinates?" hook. The point itself stays visible. Default false.

occludeTangent.description: Hide this point's tangent equation as "?" — the "find the equation of the tangent" hook. The tangent line still draws. Default false.

highlight.description: Draw the point (and its readout) in amber — result/emphasis. Default false.

lines.description: Straight lines drawn across the window; the model derives and marks where each meets the circle.

expr.description: A straight-line equation: "y = 2x + 1", "y = -x + 5", "x = 3" (vertical), "2x + 3y = 12". The intersection point(s) with the circle are derived by solving the quadratic.

label.description: Text drawn along the line (defaults to the equation). Omit to label it with its own equation; set "" for no label.

showIntersections.description: Mark the point(s) where the line meets the circle, with coordinate readouts. Default true.

occludeIntersections.description: Hide the intersection coordinates as "(?, ?)" — the "find where the line meets the circle" hook. The points still mark. Default false.

highlight.description: Draw this line in amber. Default false.

tangentForm.description: Which written form of a derived tangent equation to show. "gradient-intercept" → y = mx + c (default; m, c as exact fractions, with the special cases x = k and y = k for vertical/horizontal tangents). "normal" → the integer form px + qy = c. "both" → both, stacked.

showTangentEquation.description: Show the equation beside every drawn tangent. Default true (use point.occludeTangent to hide one as a question).

showEquation.description: Show the circle's equation. Default true.

occludeEquation.description: Hide the circle's equation as "?" — the "what is the equation of this circle?" hook. Default false.

showRadiusLength.description: Label each drawn radius with its length r. Default false.

header.description: Optional short title centred above the figure.

caption.description: Optional line centred below the figure, e.g. a short context note. Never the question or an instruction: that wording is the block's text.

draggable.description: Web-only. Each point gets a handle pupils can drag to SLIDE it around the circle; the radius, the tangent, its equation and the right-angle mark all recompute live. The point stays on the circle. Default false.
